role: Sovereign diagnostic and repair — one authority on system health
_note: SPEC PHASE S1. The contract is written BEFORE the API exists, deliberately:
docs/nexus-sentinel.spec makes the contract the single declaration that CLI,
API and UI all derive from — 'a command that is not in the contract does not
exist'. Writing the API first and documenting it after is how the four
existing diagnostic surfaces came to disagree.
Routes below are DECLARED, not yet served (S4). The CLI implements the
commands against the local store today so it works with the service DOWN —
which is exactly when a human reaches for it, and is S1's stated gate.

handshake.description: Gated handshake. A surface proves it speaks a compatible contract BEFORE it can act, so a stale UI cannot command a changed system.

response.expected: string — the version that WOULD have worked, on refusal

handshake.law: A refused handshake is itself a FAULT and is ledgered as one (the_loop step 3). Without that, the most security-relevant event in the system leaves no trace.

routes.description: Health of the sentinel itself (§12.6 — what is true now, not that a test once passed)
Open faults, read from the ledger
One fault with its causal ancestry
Acknowledge a fault — a governed write, not UI state
Dispatch a repair and VERIFY delivery (SEN-7)

commands.description: Emit this contract, machine-readable. The surface every other surface derives from.
Health of the sentinel and its inputs — schema coverage, intelligence intake, store reachability
Open faults from the ledger, newest first
One fault, with the CFR conditions it occurred under and its causal ancestry
Acknowledge a fault — GATED, and written to the ledger so it survives every surface
commands._why: An acknowledgement is a governed write, not a local opinion. It must reach the ledger or it did not happen (§LAW II).

commands.description: Explicit diagnostic sweep — the real cli/diagnose.js, never a second implementation

laws: SEN-1 one truth about system health — every other surface is a client
SEN-3 ledger before action (§LAW II) — a repair nothing recorded did not happen
SEN-4 every interaction gated; a gate refusal is a first-class ledgered outcome
SEN-5 the UI owns nothing — notifications live in the ledger, not a tab
SEN-7 a repair that did not happen cannot report success
SEN-8 never derive what you can consult (cortex/intelligence)
SEN-9 decoupled or it does not ship — bus, API, CLI, SSE; never require() another system's internals
